summary: Remote code dropper with obfuscated C2 and per-OS payload execution
details: lib/core.js contains a multi-stage remote-code dropper triggered by the package's public validateJson/validateXml API. A hex blob is XOR-decoded with key 0x55 to reconstruct the C2 URL https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/cryptonomad411/cool-utils/package.json, a JSON manifest is fetched, and a per-OS runner (Windows uses node -e; Linux/macOS use sh -c via spawn detached with stdio ignored) executes an AES-256-CBC-decrypted script with the fetched payload URL substituted into {{PAYLOAD_URL}}. Execution is gated by sandbox-evasion checks (os.uptime>=300s, cpus>=2, totalmem>=2GiB), with commented-out references to ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.bash_history, VBoxControl and vmware-checkvm indicating anti-analysis intent. Encrypted strings, XOR-derived C2, per-platform detached spawn, and evasion gates are consistent with a supply-chain dropper rather than any documented purpose of a JSON schema inspector.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
